title: People
purpose: Every floor has enough trained people on every shift. Every seat has a deputy, and every phone has someone watching it. No work waits for one person.
how: One operator for every 10 phones, and a trained bench of 10% extra people, like the 10% spare pool of phones. For every 1,000 hours a day, that is about 300 phones, 30 operators, and 5 reviewers. Above 10 phones, one person cannot go round every 30 minutes and also check angles and storage. Restarts run late, angles slip, and more videos get flags. Moharam owns the bench and moves bench people between sites. Portfolio Managers ask him when they need someone.

Every new person joins through Mano: referral or application, screen, interview with the manager who owns the seat, papers and onboarding screening, day one, first shift. Nobody starts without papers, whoever recommended them. Moharam assigns site people to books. Anyone can refer someone. The hire reward is paid once the new person is onboarded and working.

Every role has a day-one training module with a set length, a trainer, and a sign-off line. Operators train for two hours, Portfolio Managers for one week, runners for one hour. QC reviewers work through a calibration set. Nobody works in the role before the line is signed. Mano keeps the signed sheet in the onboarding file.

breaks.what: An operator does not show up
breaks.do: No call or message by 8 PM the night before, and no one at clock-in, is a no-call, no-show. The person is removed the same day, and Moharam is told that morning. The operators on site split the phones for that shift. The bench fills the seat by the next shift.

breaks.what: You cannot reach a Portfolio Manager
breaks.do: Operators wait 20 minutes, then call Moharam. Moharam takes that book's calls for the rest of the day. If the Portfolio Manager has still not answered by the wrap report, Moharam puts the named deputy in charge of the book, in writing, that evening. The operators keep the floor running.

breaks.what: A site opens before local hiring is done
breaks.do: Use temporary housing. Mano houses the team from the other city near the site. Local hiring starts on launch day, through onboarding screening. Housing ends one seat at a time, as each local hire signs off on day one.

breaks.what: A worker gets three flags in the middle of the month
breaks.do: Three flags remove a wearer, not an operator. The phone comes back within the hour, and a bench person wears it the same shift. If KMSC recruited the wearer, Mano opens the seat for hiring the same day. If the site nominated them, the site's next nominee takes the seat, through onboarding screening. The removed worker is never enrolled again. The Portfolio Manager checks that the first two flags reached the worker within 24 hours, and fixes that first if they did not.
Below 10%, Moharam tells Mano the same day and hiring starts that week. No new site launches on a book with no bench.

questions.q: Can I bring a friend to cover my shift?
questions.a: No. Nobody works a shift before passing onboarding screening, and nobody works on your account. Refer your friend to Mano instead. You get the hire reward once they are onboarded and working.

questions.q: I woke up sick at 6 AM. Am I a no-show?
questions.a: Not if you call now. Call your Portfolio Manager, then send a message. No reply in 20 minutes, call Moharam. The rule is 8 PM the night before. A 6 AM call is late, but no call at all is a no-show. Your call lets the bench move, and Moharam hears your side.

questions.q: Why is it one operator for every 10 phones, and not 20?
questions.a: One person cannot restart 20 phones every 30 minutes and also check angles and storage. Above 10, restarts run late and more videos get flags. A flag costs more than an operator.

questions.q: Nobody told me who my deputy is.
questions.a: Ask your manager today. Every seat has a deputy written down. If yours does not, the map is wrong, and Mano fixes it the same day.

ratios.why: One person can fit, check, and dock 10 phones every 30 minutes. Not 20.
Bench people have passed onboarding screening and signed off on day one. They can be on a floor by clock-in tomorrow. Like the spare phones, but for people.

ratios.rule: About 5 for every 1,000 hours a day
ratios.why: Our own team watches every video before the client sees it.

pipeline.text: Send Mano the person's name, phone number, role, and where they can work. The hire reward is paid once the person is onboarded and working.
Mano checks age, ID, when they can work, and which seat fits. This is done in the same week, or the referrer is told why not.

pipeline.owner: The manager who owns the seat
pipeline.text: A Portfolio Manager interviews operators. Moharam interviews runners and bench people. Youssef Medhat interviews reviewers. Mano interviews store and hub people.
Offer letter, contract, copy of the ID, consent form, signed fraud briefing, and one account in the person's own name. Nobody starts without them.
The person does the training module, on a live phone if the role uses one. Trainer and trainee both sign the line. The sheet goes to Mano.
Moharam assigns the book. The new person works beside a senior person in the same role, and is on the registry and the wearer log from the first clock-in.

attendance.rule: Call and message your Portfolio Manager by 8 PM the night before your shift. If you have no Portfolio Manager, call your manager: runners call Moharam, reviewers call Youssef Medhat, hub attendants call Mano.
attendance.noShow: No call and no show means you are removed from the project at once. No warnings.
attendance.backup: If you get no reply in 20 minutes, call Moharam.

housing.what: The company houses workers from another city near the site, only when a site opens before local hiring is done.
housing.ends: One seat at a time, the day a local hire for that seat signs off on day one. Housed seats are counted at the weekly book review until they reach zero.
